title: Käsespätzle (Cheese Spätzle with Crispy Onions)
summary: Egg spätzle layered with melted Emmental and alpine-style cheese, baked until bubbling and finished with deeply caramelised onions.
equipment: spätzle maker, or a colander or perforated tray with 5-6 mm holes

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 5.25 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: onions, halved and thinly sliced (about 450 g)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Cook the sliced onions in the butter and oil in a large frying pan over medium heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring more frequently as they darken, until deep golden and crisp at the edges. This slow cooking drives off the onions' water and lets their natural sugars caramelise, which is what builds the sweet, savoury flavour. Season with a pinch of salt and drain on paper towel.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, and butter the ovenproof dish, keeping it warm.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Whisk the flour, salt and nutmeg together, then in a separate jug whisk the eggs with the milk. Beat the egg mixture into the flour with a wooden spoon for 2-3 minutes, until smooth, thick and elastic, dropping slowly off the spoon in ribbons and showing small bubbles - this is what gives the dumplings enough structure to hold together.

steps.title: Rest the batter
steps.text: Leave the batter to rest for 20 minutes before cooking.

steps.title: Cook the spätzle
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to a simmer with the 32 g salt. Working in 3 batches, press the batter through a spätzle maker, or through a colander held over the pot with a spatula. They're ready about 1 minute after they float; cook 30 seconds more, then lift out with a slotted spoon and drain well.

steps.title: Layer with cheese
steps.text: As each batch of spätzle is drained, tip it straight into the warm buttered dish and scatter over a third of the mixed Emmental and alpine-style cheese. Layering while the pasta is still hot means each batch melts its share of cheese as you go, rather than everything sitting on top cold.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 8-10 minutes, until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling across the top.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Scatter the crispy onions, chives and black pepper over the top and serve immediately, while the cheese is still molten.

tips: Give the onions the full 25-30 minutes over gentle heat - rushing them with high heat browns the outside before the inside softens and sweetens.
Layer the spätzle into the dish while still warm from draining, so the cheese between each layer melts properly instead of sitting in cold clumps.
Beat the batter until it ribbons off the spoon slowly; a thin, runny batter won't hold its shape in the water.
Grate the cheese yourself rather than using pre-grated if possible, as it melts more evenly into smooth layers.
storage: Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a 180°C oven, covered with foil, until the cheese is molten again and the dish is piping hot throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
